title: Phase 3 · Stage 9: Things that might not be there
summary: Use nullable types on purpose: books that are not shelved yet, members with no loans, and lookups that find nothing.

steps.title: null is a value you plan for
body: Shelfwise already meets *nothing* everywhere: `catalog.Find` returns `Book?`, a loan's `ReturnedOn` is a `DateOnly?`, `Console.ReadLine()` returns `string?`. With nullable reference types on (they are, in every dojo program), the `?` is a **promise in the type**: *this might be null, and the compiler will warn you if you forget*.
New in this stage: a book may sit on a shelf, or not be shelved yet. That is a `string?` property, not an empty string pretending to be a value:
public string? Shelf { get; private set; }
string? title = catalog.Find(isbn)?.Title;                              // ?. : stop at null
if (last is null) return "(nothing yet)";                               // is null : the clear test
| `a ?? b` | `a`, unless it is null, then `b` |
| `a?.B` | `a.B`, or null if `a` is null (no exception) |
| `a is null` / `is not null` | the honest null check (cannot be fooled by an overloaded `==`) |
| `a!` | *trust me, it is not null*: silences the warning, checks nothing. Use rarely. |
Chains compose: `catalog.Find(loan.Isbn)?.Title ?? loan.Isbn` means *the title if the book exists, otherwise the raw ISBN*.

steps.explain: `?.` on a null gives null, so `missing?.Length` is an `int?` with no value, and `?? -1` replaces it.

steps.prompt: Which of these can be `null` without a compiler warning?
steps.explain: Only the `?` type admits null. `string shelf = null;` compiles with a warning, and the value types `int` and `DateOnly` cannot be null at all unless written `int?` and `DateOnly?`.

steps.prompt: Complete the line so it prints the borrower's name, or `?` when the member is gone.
steps.explain: `member?.Name` is null when `member` is, and `??` supplies the fallback.

steps.title: Shelves, book info and member info
prompt: 1. `Book` gets `public string? Shelf { get; private set; }` (null at first) and `public void MoveTo(string? shelf)`: a blank or null shelf clears it, anything else is trimmed and upper-cased.

2. `shelve <isbn> <shelf>` prints `The Hobbit is now on shelf A3`. `shelve <isbn>` alone clears it: `The Hobbit is no longer on a shelf`. No words or more than two: `Error: use shelve <isbn> [shelf]`. Unknown ISBN: `Error: no book with ISBN 999`.
The Hobbit by J.R.R. Tolkien (1937, Fiction)
On loan to: Ada Lovelace, due 2026-03-23
On loan to: Grace Hopper, due 2026-03-16 (overdue)
with `Shelf: (not shelved)` when there is none, and one `On loan to` line per active loan of that book, in loan order.
4. `member <id>` prints (no id: `Error: use member <id>`; unknown: `Error: no member with id 9`):
*Last borrowed* is the book of that member's most recent loan (returned or not), or `(nothing yet)`.
5. `help`: `Commands: add, list, find, info, shelve, authors, join, members, member, lend, return, loans, policies, today, advance, fines, pay, stats, fine, help, quit`.

public Book? Find(string isbn) => _byIsbn.TryGetValue(isbn, out var book) ? book : null;

require.message: Uses ?. to step through something that might be null

hints: `MoveTo` is one line: `Shelf = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(shelf) ? null : shelf.Trim().ToUpperInvariant();`.
For `info`, collect the lines in a `List<string>` and `return string.Join("\n", output);`. The shelf line is `$"Shelf: {book.Shelf ?? "(not shelved)"}"`.
For *Last borrowed*, loop over `loans` and keep `Loan? last` pointing at the latest one for that member. Then `last is null ? "(nothing yet)" : catalog.Find(last.Isbn)?.Title ?? last.Isbn`.
